answer: A Sybil swarm must first post a timber bond, then survive a grove of verifiers probing memory-bus latency: each node commits 64 GB of pinned RAM, and peers demand nanosecond access budgets, roughly 80 ns per cache-line read, across pseudo-random offsets. Passing requires a cipher proof of sequential access; failing burns the bond, about $900 per identity, so 10,000 fake agents cost $9M and 640 TB of RAM.
